# Registry Stack

> Registry Stack is a set of open-source products that let government registries answer questions and share proof of facts while records stay with the authority that holds them. Every product is free to self-host under Apache-2.0; Aubex Consulting LLC, the team behind OpenSPP, provides commercial support and packaged governance.

## Pages

- [Home](https://registrystack.org/): Overview of Registry Stack and how it fits a registry you already run.
- [The problem](https://registrystack.org/problem/): The registry failures Registry Stack is built around: over-sharing by default, safeguards on paper, and integrations that do not compound.
- [Evidence Gateway](https://registrystack.org/solutions/evidence-gateway/): Share proof of a fact, not the underlying record, with a service that needs it.
- [Protected Registry APIs](https://registrystack.org/solutions/protected-registry-apis/): Open an existing registry safely for approved services, with scoped, read-only access.
- [Registry Relay](https://registrystack.org/relay/): Protected APIs over the files and tables a registry already lives in.
- [Registry Notary](https://registrystack.org/notary/): Signed answers and wallet credentials for what a registry can attest.
- [Registry Manifest](https://registrystack.org/manifest/): Portable, standards-facing metadata describing a registry service.
- [Pricing](https://registrystack.org/pricing/): Self-host every product free under Apache-2.0, or subscribe for packaged support and governance across many registry services.
- [Start a pilot](https://registrystack.org/pilot/): What a scoped pilot looks like: one registry, its first questions live, safeguards from the first request.
- [Security](https://registrystack.org/security/): The security model: what it protects, what a deployment can reach, and the threat model in and out of scope.
- [FAQ](https://registrystack.org/faq/): Short answers to the questions program teams, security reviewers, and engineers ask first.

## Related sites

- [Documentation](https://docs.registrystack.org/): Technical reference and specifications for the Registry Stack products.
- [Live demo](https://lab.registrystack.org/): A hosted lab running the full stack on synthetic data only.
